why: A request whose target cannot be read from syntax is published, never dropped —
dropping it turns an unknown into a false certainty in the direction that makes
the report look better. But not every unresolvable request is an unresolved
ROUTE: a presigned PUT to object storage and an outbound webhook to a customer's
endpoint are requests with no route of ours behind them at all.
So each site is read once and recorded here with what it actually calls. The
generator refuses an entry whose site no longer exists, so a deleted or moved
call cannot leave a stale exemption behind.
OBJECT_STORE          — presigned upload/download against the storage provider.
EXTERNAL_DESTINATION  — an outbound call to a third party or a customer endpoint.
PROP_CALLBACK         — a handler passed as a prop; the path lives where the
handler is defined and is counted there.
LOCAL_NEXT_ROUTE      — a Next.js route handler in the web app, not an API route.
OPERATOR_TOOL         — a script whose target origin is supplied per run.

entries.evidence: fetch(res.upload.putUrl, { method: "PUT" }) — the presigned URL returned by the intake upload-session response; the storage provider, not this API.

tryDownloadFile(url, originalFileName) — url is the signed download URL returned by GET /v1/evidence/:id/original; the storage provider serves it. Both arguments are hoisted identifiers, so the analyzer resolves the call shape and reports precisely why the value is not static: it is a runtime signed URL and cannot be.

tryDownloadFile(packageUrl, packageFileName) — packageUrl is the signed verification-package URL returned by GET /v1/evidence/:id/verification-package; the storage provider serves it. Hoisted to an identifier so the analyzer resolves the call shape.
